ctor.rationale: `base(2, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (Catastrophe.cs:16-19) == cost 2 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF. No keywords.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new CardsVar(2)` (Catastrophe.cs:14) == `_cards = 2`, read as `IntValue` for the loop bound.

OnPlay.rationale: This is one of the more carefully ported cards in the pool and it holds up. Per iteration C# takes `PileType.Draw.GetPile(Owner).Cards.Where(!Unplayable).ToList().StableShuffle(Rng.Shuffle).FirstOrDefault()`, falling back to the UNFILTERED pile shuffled the same way when the filtered list is empty (Catastrophe.cs:25-30). The sim reproduces all four subtleties: it uses the named `Shuffle` stream via `stable_shuffled_cards(options, ctx.combat.combat_rng)`; it reverses the draw pile to the game's TOP-FIRST orientation first (colorless_skills.py:155) because StableShuffle's stabilising `list2.Sort()` leaves compare-equal cards in incoming order (ListExtensions.cs:22-31); it takes `[0]` after the shuffle rather than one uniform choice, so the draw COUNT matches (N-1 draws per pick); and `options = playable or pile` (colorless_skills.py:157) is exactly C#'s FirstOrDefault-null fallback. `is_playable` mirrors the Unplayable keyword.

guards.what: the sim breaks the pick loop on `ctx.combat.is_over or ctx.player.is_dead` (colorless_skills.py:152-153); Catastrophe.cs has NO loop-level bail-out
guards.issue: C#'s loop runs the full `CardsVar` iterations unconditionally. The combat-over check lives one level down, in `CardCmd.AutoPlay`'s `if (CombatManager.Instance.IsOverOrEnding || card.Owner.Creature.IsDead) return;` (CardCmd.cs:53-56) -- which is AFTER Catastrophe has already done the StableShuffle pick for that iteration. So when an auto-played card ends the combat, C# still burns a full StableShuffle (N-1 Shuffle draws) for every remaining iteration and the sim burns none. Under seed parity a differing draw COUNT is an observable desync, which is the same reasoning creature_card_cmds step 104 applies to the auto-select shortcut. LIVE: Catastrophe is a ported Uncommon colorless Skill, killing the last enemy with an auto-played Attack on the first of two or three iterations is ordinary play, and the Shuffle parity stream is wired (combat_rng.py:17,50). Note this is the OPPOSITE polarity to card/beat_down's target-roll guard, where the sim is the one that skips a draw C# takes -- both are stream-count divergences at an auto-play boundary.

guards.what: each pick re-reads the draw pile, so a card auto-played in iteration 1 cannot be picked again in iteration 2
guards.rationale: C# re-evaluates `PileType.Draw.GetPile(Owner).Cards` inside the loop (Catastrophe.cs:25) and the sim rebuilds `pile` from `ctx.player.draw_pile` each iteration (colorless_skills.py:155). Both also see any card the auto-play ADDED to the draw pile.
